column1: # neurofedora real-data pipeline manifest
# Format (TAB separated, # = comment):
#   <pkg>
# Commands run with cwd = tests/, so use $FIX (the absolute fixtures dir)
# to reference fixtures portably. $TMP is a per-test tmpdir (auto-cleaned).
# Each row becomes a BATS @test that:
#   1. skips if <pkg> isn't installed (so partial installs are graceful),
#   2. runs the command,
#   3. matches <expected pattern> (POSIX regex) against combined stdout+stderr.
# Empty <expected> = "just require exit 0".
# A leading + on a pkg name means "skip if any of these alternative packages
# are missing"  (not yet implemented — placeholder for future multi-pkg pipes).
# Mark in-progress / known-failing rows with `# WIP:` to disable.

column1: # fsleyes render uses GLX even in headless mode — needs a real X display.
# We accept SKIP (no xvfb-run) or a successful render (file >= 1 KB).
python3-fsleyes
column2: command -v xvfb-run >/dev/null || { echo "SKIP: xvfb-run missing"; exit 0; }; out="$TMP/render.png"; timeout 45 xvfb-run -a fsleyes render -of "$out" "$FIX/t1.nii.gz" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; sz=$(wc -c <"$out" 2>/dev/null || echo 0); [ "$sz" -gt 1000 ] && echo "rendered $sz bytes" || echo "RENDER_EMPTY size=$sz"

# ── ANTs real-data systems tests (added 2026-08) ───────────────────────────
# These go beyond "did the binary run": each asserts a quantitative property
# of the OUTPUT on the real MNI152 2 mm template, so a silently-miscompiled
# ANTs (bad ITK, wrong BLAS, broken optimizer) fails here even though the
# smoke tests pass. Threads are pinned via ITK_GLOBAL_DEFAULT_NUMBER_OF_THREADS
# to keep them deterministic and CI-friendly.
# N4 bias-field correction must produce a same-grid corrected volume.
ANTs
column2: ITK_GLOBAL_DEFAULT_NUMBER_OF_THREADS=2 N4BiasFieldCorrection -d 3 -i "$FIX/real/mni152_t1_2mm.nii.gz" -x "$FIX/real/mni152_brain_mask_2mm.nii.gz" -o "$TMP/n4.nii.gz" -c '[20x10,1e-4]' -s 4 >/dev/null 2>&1 && python3 -c "import nibabel as nib; print('N4_OK shape=', nib.load('$TMP/n4.nii.gz').shape)"

column1: # Atropos k-means must find exactly 3 tissue classes (+0 background) inside the
# brain mask. A broken segmentation collapses classes and changes this list.
ANTs
column2: ITK_GLOBAL_DEFAULT_NUMBER_OF_THREADS=2 Atropos -d 3 -a "$FIX/real/mni152_t1_2mm.nii.gz" -x "$FIX/real/mni152_brain_mask_2mm.nii.gz" -i kmeans[3] -c '[3,0]' -m '[0.1,1x1x1]' -o "$TMP/seg.nii.gz" >/dev/null 2>&1 && python3 -c "import nibabel as nib, numpy as np; print('ATROPOS_LABELS', np.unique(nib.load('$TMP/seg.nii.gz').get_fdata().astype(int)).tolist())"

column1: # FLAGSHIP correctness test: the _moved fixture is the template shifted by a
# known 2-voxel offset. Rigid registration must measurably RECOVER it — mutual
# information (more negative = better) must improve by a wide margin. Observed:
# -0.478 (misaligned) -> -0.893 (registered), i.e. back to the self-similarity
# baseline of -0.8934. This catches an ANTs whose optimizer/metric is broken
# even though every binary still exits 0. Runtime ~2 min.
ANTs
column2: export ITK_GLOBAL_DEFAULT_NUMBER_OF_THREADS=2; F="$FIX/real/mni152_t1_2mm.nii.gz"; M="$FIX/real/mni152_t1_2mm_moved.nii.gz"; B=$(MeasureImageSimilarity -d 3 -m "MI[$F,$M,1,32]" 2>/dev/null | tail -1); antsRegistrationSyN.sh -d 3 -f "$F" -m "$M" -o "$TMP/reg_" -t r -n 2 >/dev/null 2>&1; A=$(MeasureImageSimilarity -d 3 -m "MI[$F,$TMP/reg_Warped.nii.gz,1,32]" 2>/dev/null | tail -1); python3 -c "b=float('$B'); a=float('$A'); print('MI_IMPROVED' if a < b - 0.05 else 'MI_NOT_IMPROVED', round(b,4), round(a,4))"

column1: # ─── Real DWI section (dipy.fetch_sherbrooke_3shell → fixtures/real/dwi/) ─
# HARDI 150-direction 3-shell dataset, ~184 MB. Provides real .nii.gz +
# matching .bval + .bvec. Exercises every neuroimaging tool's DWI loader
# against a non-synthetic acquisition. SKIPs cleanly if dipy isn't
# installed (fetch-real-fixtures.sh's Section 6 only runs when dipy is
# importable). Pipelines that need real DWI use $FIX/real/dwi/HARDI193.*
# nibabel: bare NIfTI load + bvec parse (canonical Python DWI smoke).
# Note: dipy's HARDI193.bvec is stored as (193, 3) — directions × xyz —
# NOT the FSL canonical (3, 193). np.loadtxt reads it as-is; tools that
# need FSL layout (.bvec = 3 rows × N cols) must transpose.
python3-nibabel
column2: python3 -c 'import nibabel as nb, numpy as np; img=nb.load("$FIX/real/dwi/HARDI193.nii.gz"); bvec=np.loadtxt("$FIX/real/dwi/HARDI193.bvec"); print("shape", img.shape, "bvec", bvec.shape)'
